title.value: Semantic Membership Inference Attack against Large Language Models

abstract.value: Membership Inference Attacks (MIAs) determine whether a specific data point was included in the training set of a target model. In this paper, we introduce the Semantic Membership Inference Attack (SMIA), a novel approach that enhances MIA performance by leveraging the semantic content of inputs and their perturbations. SMIA trains a neural network to analyze the target model’s behavior on perturbed inputs, effectively capturing variations in output probability distributions between members and non-members. We conduct comprehensive evaluations on the Pythia and GPT-Neo model families using the Wikipedia and MIMIR datasets. Our results show that SMIA significantly outperforms existing MIAs; for instance, for Wikipedia, SMIA achieves an AUC-ROC of 67.39\% on Pythia-12B, compared to 58.90\% by the second-best attack.
